articleTitle: Certain aspects of automation applied to power station operations
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In recent years we have seen how automation has taken increasing possession of the plant control sector of our power stations. The Initial controversies on the approach to automation have now given way to more concrete solutions. Manufacturers and power station companies have now benefited by the experience gathered from a large number of automated plants and are better able to correlate the mechanical and operational aspects involved. This paper outlines the result of six years’ experience of thermal power plant automation in Germany.

abstract: The expression ‘dc transmission’ is an all-embracing term with many facets, including power system engineering, converter stations design, special equipment design, and like all engineering it is greatly influenced by economics. In essence, a dc transmission scheme will draw its power from some ac source — either directly from generators or alternatively from a power system which in itself can have varying degrees of complexity — and after rectification, transmission and inversion feed the power into another ac system, again of varying complexity, or into another part of the same system. The dc transmission system has to be assessed in terms of economics and reliability compared with alternative ac methods of transmission.

articleTitle: The control of processes in thin-film circuit manufacture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The in-house facilities of the CSIR manufacturing thin-film integrated circu’ts are described. Resistive NiCr layers are deposited from separate Ni and Cr electron gun sources, which allow the production of resistive layers with small temperature coefficients and high stability. Each source is incorporated in a closed feedback loop to achieve a constant deposition rate. The quartz crystal and a novel ultrasonic monitor are briefly described, as well as the manufacturing steps of mask-making, deposition, component adjustment, bonding incorporating active devices, testing and encapsulation of a circuit. The layout of a small plant is presented. The maximum and minimum values of components which can be made in thin-film technique, and the relative merits of the thin-film and other techniques for manufacturing integrated circuits, are discussed.

articleTitle: The history and performance of a radar parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Research on parametric amplifiers in the National Institute for Telecommunications Research led to the development of a practical amplifier at 600 MHz. This amplifier has been successfully applied to operational radars and has been described elsewhere1, 2. The amplifier has now completed six years of continuous 24-hour service on the airport radar at Jan Smuts Airport, Johannesburg, and will shortly be ‘retired’ when the new airport radar, which is now being installed, is commissioned in about September 1968. This amplifier was one of the first parametric amplifiers to be integrated with an operational radar anywhere in the world, and in view of its remarkable achievement of trouble-free and continuous service, as well as its resulting improvement of eight times in radar system temperature, it was considered that the history and performance of this amplifier were worth recording.

abstract: In 1959 Texas Instruments developed the first IC, a laboratory model. abstract: D. Kennealy (Associate Member) I would like to thank the authors for their comprehensive survey of the available methods of producing variable speed electric drives for industry. So often in our very technical papers we get lost in a welter of detail on a particular drive and the student of electrical engineering and also the not-so-well versed industrial user quite often cannot see the wood for the trees. A wide-ranging paper of this nature from time to time therefore does a lot of good by refreshing everyone's memories. I think the paper's value would have been enhanced if the authors had not only described the numerous systems, both past and present, but had gone into greater detail as to why some of the methods have found limited application whilst others have been more and more applied and refined.

articleTitle: Modern developments in variable speed drives
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper starts with a review of methods of obtaining variable speed outputs from electrical machines that have been used in the past, and discusses the implications of the addition of closed loop control.
